open_points.subject: flow constants in compose_flow_version
open_points.text: Inputs: A flow name, a purpose when new, ports, nodes, edges, guards, constants with declared classes, the actor. ... A constant's StoredValue takes the value_schema and class the composing agent declared with it (State 6, decision 5)
open_points.question: Where does each constant's declared value_schema come from, since the operation inputs mention only its declared class?
options: Each constant explicitly supplies value_schema
The target port supplies the schema
The kernel infers the schema from the literal
open_points.default_guess: Require every constant to supply its value_schema explicitly.

open_points.subject: caller-supplied derived identities and manifest-owned binding fields
open_points.text: A request that supplies one of these identities is refused. ... an unknown field ... is refused [during surface schema validation]. ... The proposer states no effect class and no key fields; a request that does is refused
open_points.question: Are forbidden identity, effect_class and idempotency-key fields recognized request fields that reach the owning module and return refused, or unknown fields rejected by surface as invalid_request?
options: Reject them at surface as invalid_request
Accept them in the request schema solely to return refused from the owning module
Use different handling for identities and binding-owned fields
open_points.default_guess: Treat every field absent from the public operation's Inputs as an unknown field and return invalid_request.

open_points.subject: refusal and proof failure reasons
open_points.text: refuses with one code ... and a bounded reason naming the first failing check ... ProofResult M17: ... the first failure with phase, node or edge and reason
open_points.question: What exact stable values or format identify each failing check and proof reason?
options: Closed symbolic reason identifiers
Free-form bounded prose
A symbolic identifier plus bounded explanatory prose
open_points.default_guess: Use stable symbolic identifiers plus optional bounded explanatory prose.

open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_deadline
open_points.text: Outputs: A monotonic deadline and a way to ask whether it passed.
open_points.question: What object or operations constitute the deadline and the 'way to ask', and may callers inspect or compare its underlying value?
options: An opaque deadline object with an expired operation
A numeric monotonic timestamp
A callback or predicate supplied with the deadline
open_points.default_guess: Return an opaque deadline object exposing only an expiration check.

open_points.subject: timestamps written in one store change
open_points.text: every other time when its store change is made
open_points.question: When one transaction writes several timestamp fields, are they all assigned one shared clock reading or may each field receive a separate reading?
options: One clock reading shared by the whole store change
One reading per record
One reading per timestamp field
open_points.default_guess: Use one clock reading for all timestamps representing the same store change.

open_points.subject: manifest revision access
open_points.text: The kernel reads a service's record only from <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision
open_points.question: How is a file read 'at' manifest_revision: from an already checked-out immutable directory, through a version-control repository lookup, or by another revision-addressing mechanism?
options: manifest_location is already an immutable checkout of the configured revision
The kernel resolves manifest_revision through version control
manifest_location provides a revision-aware storage API
open_points.default_guess: Treat manifest_location as a repository and read the file from the exact configured revision without changing the working tree.

open_points.subject: JSON HTTP request content type
open_points.text: for POST, PUT and PATCH they form one JSON object body keyed by port name ... with a body, content-type and content-length
open_points.question: What exact Content-Type value is sent for a non-multipart JSON body?
options: application/json
application/json; charset=utf-8
A manifest-required value

open_points.subject: multipart/form-data wire encoding
open_points.text: a multipart/form-data body with one part per other input port ... Each part has exactly two headers ... the multipart/form-data content type without its boundary parameter
open_points.question: What exact multipart serialization is used, including boundary generation, CRLF layout, header quoting and escaping, and final-boundary form?
options: A fixed kernel-defined canonical multipart encoding
Any RFC-compliant encoding
The HTTP library's native multipart encoder
open_points.default_guess: Define and use one kernel-owned canonical RFC-compliant multipart encoding with a freshly chosen safe boundary.

open_points.subject: transport timeout interval
open_points.text: a response is used only when ... it arrived within transport_timeout_ms ... send once, within the transport deadline
open_points.question: When does transport_timeout_ms start, and does it cover DNS resolution, connection, TLS, request upload and the complete response body?
options: It starts immediately before DNS and covers the entire attempt
It starts after request preparation but before connection
Separate internal phases receive portions of the timeout
open_points.default_guess: Start one deadline immediately before DNS resolution and apply it to the entire network attempt through the last response byte.

open_points.subject: HTTP failure_detail construction
open_points.text: at most failure_detail_bytes_max of [the error response body] is kept as failure_detail
open_points.question: How are arbitrary response bytes converted to the textual failure_detail, and is truncation applied before or after decoding?
options: Require UTF-8 and replace invalid sequences
Decode UTF-8 strictly and omit detail on failure
Encode arbitrary bytes as base64 or hexadecimal
open_points.default_guess: Take the bounded byte prefix, back up to a UTF-8 boundary, and decode with invalid sequences replaced.

open_points.subject: sandbox failure_detail construction
open_points.text: only for the exception type and message, never stdout ... a bounded failure_detail otherwise
open_points.question: What exact failure_detail is returned for Python exceptions, load failures, abnormal exits, limit failures and sandbox traps?
options: Closed symbolic details for non-exception failures and a fixed type/message format for exceptions
Implementation-defined bounded prose
Only the exception message or fixed outcome name
open_points.default_guess: Use closed symbolic details for kernel-detected failures and a fixed '<exception-type>: <message>' format for Python exceptions.

open_points.subject: filtered record pagination
open_points.text: Outputs: Up to the page size of records ... and the next continuation token when more remain. ... The filter is applied as of each page's request: a record whose filtered field changed since an earlier page is judged by its value now
open_points.question: For a filtered page containing fewer than page_size matches, does 'more remain' mean more matching records now or any lower store positions that might match on a later request, and what position anchors an empty filtered page?
options: Issue a token only when another matching record currently exists
Scan page_size store positions and issue a token while any lower position exists
Use an immutable snapshot of filter membership
open_points.default_guess: Page by scanned store positions and return a token while lower store positions remain, even if the current page has no matches.

open_points.subject: MCP listen address and entrance opening
open_points.text: mcp_listen_address: where the one mcp entrance listens ... Outputs: A serving kernel; or a stopped start: the failing step and its reason
open_points.question: What forms of listen address are valid, when is the socket bound in the start sequence, and what happens if parsing, binding or listening fails?
options: Validate during installation loading and bind only after recovery
Validate and bind before recovery but accept requests only afterward
Delegate parsing and binding entirely to the MCP host runtime
open_points.default_guess: Validate at installation loading, complete recovery, then bind before reporting the kernel as serving; a bind failure stops start with a sanitized reason.
